[LGRA.9.8.10] **Clock functions.** `now() → Time` returns the wall-clock
instant ([LTIM.2.1.1]) and `monotonic_ns() → Duration` the monotonic clock's
reading ([LTIM.2.2.1]). Unlike the read functions ([LGRA.9.8.2]), each may
appear in any expression position — a `where` clause, an action argument,
anywhere in a `let` RHS — except an interpolation body, which takes a path and
not a call ([LGRA.2.9.6.9]). In a `where` clause either makes the condition
time-dependent ([LTIM.2.4.1]). A `let` whose entire RHS is a clock read binds
the value once per activation; multiple references to the let name reuse that
single value rather than re-reading the clock. (See the let purity tiers
below.)

**That reuse is an optimisation, not a second semantics.**
[LTIM.2.1.3] already fixes one clock value for the whole
activation — activations are atomic with respect to the
clock — so two separate `let`s each binding `now()` take
the **same** value, and re-reading would be permitted to
change nothing. This clause says when the engine *may*
skip the read; [LTIM.2.1.3] says what the read must
return.
